task.text: Each widget holds references to the others, so every new rule edits all of them.
Introduce a **mediator**. `SignupForm` and its widgets must keep behaving exactly as they do now.

items: `TextBox`, `Checkbox` and `Button` each get a constructor taking a `Dialog`, keep it in one `private final` field, and report to it when the user acts (`type`, `toggle`, `click`).
Widgets keep their own state and methods, but no widget may reference another widget type.
`SignupForm` owns the rules (when Submit is enabled, what a click does) and keeps its fields and `sent()`.

checks.title: A new form starts empty and disabled
Submit needs a name and accepted terms
Submit sends the name and resets the form
The form can be submitted twice
Widgets report their changes to any Dialog

hints.text: Widgets are coupled in a many-to-many web. Route everything through one object that all of them know, and move the knowledge of who reacts to whom into that object.
Give each widget a `Dialog` instead of references to its neighbours. Let `SignupForm` implement `Dialog`: it creates the widgets with `this`, and `changed` decides what to update.
